units.title: Classify integer-valued functions under a product inequality
units.statement: The functions f:R→Z satisfying f(x)^2+f(y)^2≤2f(xy) for every real x,y are precisely f=0, f=1, and f=1 at zero and 0 elsewhere. Substitution at (0,0) gives f(0)∈{0,1}. If f(0)=0, using y=0 gives f=0. If f(0)=1, the same substitution bounds values to {-1,0,1}; using y=1 eliminates -1. A nonzero x with f(x)=1 forces f(xy)=1 for every y, so f=1. Otherwise only f(0)=1 remains.
steps: Determine f(0) from the inequality at (0,0)
Bound all values using y=0 and y=1
Use a nonzero point with value 1 to force the constant solution
